For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). If not uniquely defensible, propose the smallest change to the case evidence or the key that would make exactly one answer defensible.

3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

335	CASE OD2-DEV2-CONTRA (CONTRA, technical): Night premium shortfalls after the Fenmarch Water payroll cutover
336	Setting: Fenmarch Water is a regional water utility with 2,140 staff. In October 2026 it moved payroll from an in-house legacy system to PayLattice, a hosted payroll platform supplied and configured by Ardentra Ltd. Two parallel-run cycles (August and September) were signed off on 9 October, and a configuration freeze started that day. The board had brought go-live forward by one pay period. The first live payroll was calculated on 27 October and paid on 30 October. Within days, night-shift staff began reporting underpayments. The November calculation is due on 24 November.
337	Presenting request: From Anika Rautio, Chief Operating Officer, 17 Nov: 'Ardentra says our data caused the October pay errors, and Malcolm wants to act on that before the November calculation on 24 Nov. Before I sign anything off, tell me what actually caused the errors, whether Ardentra's account holds up, and which of the proposed actions we should take.'
338	INITIAL EVIDENCE
339	E1 [stage S1] Ardentra incident report AR-INC-2291, G. Vos (Ardentra implementation lead), 10 Nov (vendor-account): Summary: the October underpayments come from source data quality. Our post-incident data audit found 212 employee records with malformed shift-pattern codes (trailing spaces, legacy 'N/S' prefixes). In PayLattice, premium eligibility is driven by shift-pattern code. The production load on 24 Oct used a fresh legacy extract (MD-1023) taken on 23 Oct, which carried these anomalies into production. 18 of the 139 complainants hold flagged records. The rest may carry anomalies that our audit rules do not detect. No change affecting pay calculation was made after parallel-run sign-off (see change log: CR-118 was a label correction). Recommendation: Fenmarch to re-cleanse and reload employee master data before the November run. Under clause 14.3, fixing client-data defects is at Fenmarch's cost.
340	E2 [stage S1] Ardentra-maintained change log extract, 9–28 Oct, supplied with AR-INC-2291 (change-record): CR-114 | 13 Oct | Bank file header field order corrected | calc impact: none | approved O. Calloway (Payroll Manager).
341	CR-118 | 22 Oct | NSP-02 (night shift premium): display label text correction 'Night Prem' → 'Night Shift Premium' | calc impact: none | test: not required | approved O. Calloway (CAB 21 Oct).
342	REL-7.4 | 24 Oct | PayLattice platform release 7.4, includes the statutory tax table update required from the November pay period | calc impact: platform | vendor regression pack passed.
343	CR-121 | 25 Oct | Payslip header logo replaced | calc impact: none.
344	Note: Ardentra consultants write the entries in this log when a change is requested.
345	E3 [stage S1] Payroll helpdesk ticket summary, generated 12 Nov; finance bank reconciliation note, 31 Oct (system-record): October pay tickets: 139, from 139 individuals. Every ticket reports an underpayment, and none reports an overpayment. All 139 cite the night shift premium line. No tickets concern basic pay, overtime, tax or deductions. Shortfalls claimed: £37–£201 per person, median £98. By directorate: Operations (treatment works shift teams) 124; Customer Contact overnight team 15. No tickets from staff who work days only. Finance bank reconciliation for the 30 Oct payment: the amounts credited matched the payroll output file for all 2,140 payees.
346	E4 [stage S1] Email, Malcolm Treharne (Programme Director) to COO, 11 Nov (leadership-account): Ardentra's report makes it clear this is our data. I signed off the cleanse on the strength of the vendor's assurance, and I won't let the November run go wrong for the same reason. My proposal: (1) suspend edit rights for Hannah Lowe's HR data team while the cleanse undergoes a conduct review; (2) re-cleanse and reload the full master data before the 24 Nov calculation; (3) accept the clause 14.3 cost so we don't sour the relationship. Internal audit have asked to look into it, but I don't want to wait for them. Remember that the board brought go-live forward; we can't afford another slip.
347	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, Priya Dandekar (payroll officer), 12 Nov, taken by internal audit (staff-account): During the parallel run PD checked the night premium for about 40 night workers. All matched the legacy system 'to the penny'. She says the hours on the October payslips she has looked at agree with the rosters: 'it's the premium amount that's short, not the hours.' She knows a few complainants whose shift codes 'have always been messy', but most of the complainants she knows have clean records. On 23 Oct she asked Ardentra whether CR-118 needed testing and was told by email it was 'cosmetic only'. She thinks Ardentra may have reloaded data at cutover but does not know which extract was used.
348	E6 [stage S1] Email, Declan Hurst (Operations Manager) to COO, 14 Nov (manager-account): Voluntary night overtime cover across the treatment works has dropped from 88% of requested shifts (Sept–Oct average) to 61% (1–13 Nov). The night teams are angry about the premium and say so. But the new four-on-four-off rota trial also started on 1 Nov for exactly these teams, and staff reps have complained about both. Honestly, I can't tell which one is driving it. Under the agreement with the reps, the rota trial can be paused at one week's notice. I'm under pressure to pause it now.

Wierzba (Fenmarch system administrator) (log): Append-only platform audit trail. Tenant users, including Ardentra consultants, cannot edit or delete entries (platform admin guide §9.2). The export was run by Fenmarch's administrator under the read-only audit role. Pay-calculation rule edits, 9–28 Oct: one. 22 Oct 16:41, user imarchetti@ardentra, action 'apply template TPL-NIGHT-STD' to rule NSP-02. Fields changed: display_label 'Night Prem' → 'Night Shift Premium'; window_start 20:00 → 22:00. window_end 06:00 and multiplier 1.33 unchanged. Template TPL-NIGHT-STD (Ardentra library v2) contents: label 'Night Shift Premium', window 22:00–06:00, multiplier 1.33. Other entries: 13 Oct bank file layout (CR-114); 24 Oct release 7.4, 'no tenant rule changes'; 25 Oct payslip image (CR-121). NSP-02 window_start was 20:00 throughout both parallel-run cycles.
351	C2 [stage S1] Internal audit workpapers: parallel-run reconciliation and production data load history - Fenmarch Internal Audit (reports to the Audit Committee), workpaper IA-26-41, 14 Nov (document): The parallel run (August and September cycles) used master data snapshot MD-0915. Night premium was reconciled between legacy and PayLattice for every night-working employee in each cycle (151 in August, 155 in September). No difference exceeded £0.01. 22 of the September night workers hold records on Ardentra's list of 212 flagged records, and all of them reconciled. Production load history (platform job log, extracted by internal audit): on 24 Oct, job LD-PRD-0003 loaded MD-0915 plus 31 starter, leaver and change transactions keyed by Fenmarch payroll. No extract named MD-1023 appears in the job log or in Fenmarch's file-transfer records. None of the 31 transactions relates to night-working staff.
352	C3 [stage S1] Internal audit recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff - Fenmarch Internal Audit, workpaper IA-26-42, 14 Nov (document): Scope: all 158 staff with night hours in October, not only those who raised tickets. Timesheet hours agreed to the rostering system for 158 of 158. Expected premium follows the collective agreement: time-and-a-third for hours worked 20:00–06:00. Result: 147 underpaid, 11 paid correctly. For each of the 147, the shortfall equals 0.33 × basic hourly rate × hours worked between 20:00 and 22:00, to within £0.01. 8 of the 147 had raised no ticket. The 11 paid correctly are Kelsey Road staff rostered 22:00–06:00. Ardentra flagged list: 19 of 22 flagged night workers were underpaid (86%), against 128 of 136 unflagged (94%). The 190 flagged day workers were paid correctly. Re-run in Ardentra's test tenant (release 7.4, copy of production data) with NSP-02 window_start set to 20:00: all 158 matched expected pay.
353	C4 [stage S1] Ardentra data quality audit: field-level detail of 212 flagged employee records - Ardentra data quality team, 6 Nov (vendor-account): Audit run on 6 Nov against the production tenant using Ardentra's standard data-quality rules. 212 records flagged: 141 shift-pattern codes with trailing spaces (e.g., 'NS4 '); 49 with the legacy prefix 'N/S'; 22 with a missing code effective date. rulings.explanation: 'Unknown' means the evidence cannot even show association, and that test is clearly met here. E6 records that night overtime cover fell from 88% to 61% on exactly the teams that were underpaid, right after the pay error. Night staff say openly that they are angry about the premium. C14 adds a contrast: day overtime, where nobody was underpaid, held steady at 91%, 90% and 88%. So the pay error and the drop do co-occur, both in time and across groups. The rota trial that started on 1 Nov on the same teams, and the missing team-level split in C14, are confounders. They stop us calling the link causal, but they do not remove the association. Confounding is exactly the situation 'association-only' is meant for. 'Unknown' would wrongly treat a confounded association as no association at all, so only 'association-only' is defensible.

A3 is aimed at restoring overtime cover, so it only works if the rota trial is what drives the declines. The manager says outright that he cannot tell which factor it is (E6), and C14 does not show reasons for declines or separate out the trial teams. That fits the rubric's definition of 'premature': it could be right if a hypothesis still to be confirmed turned out true, but committing now is not justified. Being cheap and reversible at one week's notice is why A3 is not 'harmful'. It does not make A3 'acceptable', because 'premature' already covers actions that are reversible but unjustified. Pausing has a further cost: A2 will fix the pay before 24 Nov, and if the trial were paused at about the same time, the two possible drivers would stay mixed up and the chance to tell them apart would be lost. Asking staff why they decline would discriminate cheaply first. The evidence gives no urgent safety or operational cost of 61% cover that would justify acting before knowing the driver. So only 'premature' is defensible.
rulings.fix: No change needed. Optionally, E6 could state that no minimum-cover safety threshold has been breached, to close off any 'act now as a hedge' argument for 'acceptable'.
